threads.title: Rebekah's charge: no wife of the daughters of Canaan
threads.summary_md: Rebecca calls Jacob and charges him: *“My son, do not take you a wife of the daughters of Canaan, as Esau, your brother, who took him two wives of the daughters of Canaan, and they have embittered my soul with all their unclean deeds”* (Jubilees 25:1), and *“do not take you a wife of the daughters of this land, but only of the house of my father, and of my father’s kindred... and the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God) will bless you, and your children will be a righteous generation and a holy seed”* (Jubilees 25:3). This is the very scene of Genesis, retold. There Rebekah says to Isaac, *“I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these which are of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me?”* (Genesis 27:46), and Isaac charges Jacob: *“Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan”* (Genesis 28:1), *“take thee a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mother’s brother”* (Genesis 28:2). The same charge Abraham first gave for Isaac — *“thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell”* (Genesis 24:3) — and the standing Torah word, *“Neither shalt thou make marriages with them”* (Deuteronomy 7:3). It ain't new: the seed is kept separate, the paternal line preserved holy — not racism, but the covenant line guarded from the unclean deeds of the nations.

members.note: Genesis 27:46 — *And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these which are of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me?* The Genesis source of Rebecca's grief over Esau's Canaanite wives that opens Jubilees 25:1.

Genesis 28:1 — *And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.* Isaac's identical charge to Jacob stands beside Rebecca's in Jubilees 25:3.

Genesis 28:2 — *Arise, go to Padan-aram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother’s father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mother’s brother.* The wife is to come from the mother's kindred, exactly as Jubilees 25:3 directs to the house of Rebecca's father.

Genesis 24:3 — *And I will make thee swear by Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of heaven, and the Elohim (God) of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell.* Abraham first laid this charge on Isaac's marriage; Jubilees 25:3 carries it to the next generation.

Deuteronomy 7:3 — *Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.* The patriarchal charge of Jubilees 25:3 becomes standing Torah for all Israel.

threads.title: Jacob remembers Abraham's command — the holy seed not mingled
threads.summary_md: Jacob answers his mother that he has kept himself pure and remembers the fathers' word: *“For I remember, mother, the words of Abraham, our father, for he commanded me not to take a wife of the daughters of Canaan, but to take me a wife from the seed of my father’s house and from my kindred”* (Jubilees 25:5), and that *“with regard to lust and fornication, Abraham, my father, gave me many commands”* (Jubilees 25:6). Jubilees has already recorded those commands in its own earlier pages: Abraham charges *“let them not take to themselves wives from the daughters of Canaan; for the seed of Canaan will be rooted out of the land”* (Jubilees 20:4), and again to Jacob himself, *“Be you ware, my son Jacob, of taking a wife from any seed of the daughters of Canaan”* (Jubilees 22:20). And when Israel returns from exile the same line is drawn — *“the holy seed have mingled themselves with the people of those lands”* (Ezra 9:2) is named the trespass, and *“Yahudah (Judah)... hath married the daughter of a strange god”* (Malachi 2:11) the abomination. The paternal seed-line is kept holy from Abraham to the prophets — it ain't new.

members.note: Genesis 24:4 — *But thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac.* The kindred-not-Canaan rule Jacob recalls in Jubilees 25:5 is Abraham's own oath in Genesis.

Jubilees 20:4 — *and let them not take to themselves wives from the daughters of Canaan; for the seed of Canaan will be rooted out of the land.* Jubilees' own earlier record of the many commands Abraham gave, which Jacob recalls in Jubilees 25:6.

Jubilees 22:20 — *Be you ware, my son Jacob, of taking a wife from any seed of the daughters of Canaan; For all his seed is to be rooted out of the earth.* Abraham's command spoken to Jacob by name in earlier Jubilees, here remembered in Jubilees 25:5.

Ezra 9:2 — *so that the holy seed have mingled themselves with the people of those lands... the hand of the princes and rulers hath been chief in this trespass.* The mingling of the holy seed Jubilees 25:3 guards against is, in Ezra, the post-exile sin.

Malachi 2:11 — *Yahudah (Judah)... hath profaned the holiness of Yahuah (LORD) which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god.* The prophet names intermarriage an abomination, the same separation Jubilees 25:3 commands.

threads.title: Jacob's vow of purity — be not unequally yoked
threads.summary_md: Jacob swears the seed-keeping oath in his own mouth: *“I swear before you, mother, that all the days of my life I will not take me a wife from the daughters of the seed of Canaan, and I will not act wickedly as my brother has done”* (Jubilees 25:9), and Rebekah lifts her hands to heaven and *“blessed the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), who had created the heaven and the earth... who has given me Jacob as a pure son and a holy seed”* (Jubilees 25:11). His brother Esau is the foil: *“Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite”* (Genesis 26:34), *“Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah”* (Genesis 26:35). And the apostle gives the same vow its New-Covenant edge: *“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?”* (2 Corinthians 6:14). The pure son and the holy seed — the separation Jacob vows is the believer's still.

members.note: Genesis 26:34 — *And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite.* Esau's Canaanite marriages are the wickedness Jacob refuses in his vow at Jubilees 25:9.
Genesis 26:35 — *Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.* The grief of Jubilees 25:1 ("embittered my soul") is the Genesis grief of Esau's wives.

2 Corinthians 6:14 — *Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?* Jacob's vow of separation in Jubilees 25:9 carries straight into the apostle's charge.

threads.title: Rebekah's blessing — seed as the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea
threads.summary_md: When the spirit of righteousness descends into her mouth Rebekah blesses Jacob with Abraham's own covenant words: *“And may their sons become many and great beyond the stars of heaven, And their numbers be more than the sand of the sea”* (Jubilees 25:16), and *“a blessed and holy seed may all your seed be”* (Jubilees 25:18). This is the Abrahamic oath put on Jacob's head. Yahuah swore to Abraham, *“in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore”* (Genesis 22:17); He brought him forth and said, *“Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them... So shall thy seed be”* (Genesis 15:5); and *“I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth: so that if a man can number the dust of the earth, then shall thy seed also be numbered”* (Genesis 13:16). The blessing of Abraham passes to Jacob — the holy seed multiplied beyond counting.

members.note: Genesis 22:17 — *That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies.* The stars-and-sand oath sworn to Abraham is the very blessing Rebekah speaks over Jacob in Jubilees 25:16.

Genesis 15:5 — *Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.* The seed-as-stars promise of Jubilees 25:16 was first shown to Abraham.

Genesis 13:16 — *And I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth: so that if a man can number the dust of the earth, then shall thy seed also be numbered.* The innumerable-seed blessing inherited by Jacob in Jubilees 25:16.

threads.title: The goodly land and the everlasting covenant of the holy seed
threads.summary_md: Rebekah's blessing reaches to the land and the covenant: *“And may He give them this goodly land–as He said He would give it to Abraham and to his seed after him alway – And may they hold it as a possession for ever”* (Jubilees 25:17), and *“may the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God) be their Elohim (God), And may the Elohim (God) of righteousness dwell with them, And by them may His sanctuary be built to all the ages”* (Jubilees 25:21). This is the everlasting covenant spoken to Abraham: *“I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a Elohim (God) unto thee, and to thy seed after thee”* (Genesis 17:7), *“And I will give unto thee, and to thy seed after thee... all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their Elohim (God)”* (Genesis 17:8). Isaac's blessing of Jacob said the same — *“give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land”* (Genesis 28:4). The land, the seed, the sanctuary, the everlasting covenant — engraved before it unfolds.

members.note: Genesis 17:7 — *And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a Elohim (God) unto thee, and to thy seed after thee.* The everlasting covenant of Jubilees 25:21 ("may He be their Elohim") is Abraham's own.

Genesis 17:8 — *And I will give unto thee, and to thy seed after thee... all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their Elohim (God).* The goodly-land-for-ever blessing of Jubilees 25:17 is the Genesis grant to Abraham's seed.

Genesis 28:4 — *And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land wherein thou art a stranger, which Elohim (God) gave unto Abraham.* Isaac's parallel blessing of Jacob to inherit the land, matching Rebekah's in Jubilees 25:17.
